newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Deputy PM sex allegation upsets Belgian markets.
newsitem.headline: Deputy PM sex allegation upsets Belgian markets.

text.p: Belgian financial markets spun lower on Monday as investors turned cautious about placing their money in the country in the wake of weekend media reports that a deputy prime minister was linked to a possible sex scandal.
Elio Di Rupo, also economics and telecommunications minister in the ruling centre-left coalition, denied the allegations, describing the reports as foolish and insulting.
Belgian shares, the Belgian franc and bonds lost ground on the reports that the minister had been named in connection with a police search for evidence of possible paedophile acts.
The Bel-20 share index was down almost seven points at 1,862.64 at 1010 GMT, while futures on government bonds lost 0.18 at 120.20. The franc fell to 20.6140/55 to the mark from 20.6075/90 on Friday.
"The first thing we heard when we opened the lines this morning was questions from abroad about the government's stability," one money market dealer said.

"We quickly assured our foreign partners they need not worry a possible sex scandal involving a top minister would somehow harm Belgium's determination to join the single currency," he said. "(Prime Minister Jean-Luc) Dehaene is still there."
Dehaene is a staunch supporter of Belgium's entry into Europe's economic and monetary union.
Dealers said the government would remain under high tension as long as Di Rupo's name was not cleared by investigators.
A share dealer said that the child sex allegation in government ranks has startled the bourse in early trading.
Others noted the concern did not just centre on the allegation against Di Rupo.
Agriculture Minister Karel Pinxten has denied allegations, made by a senior civil servant, of tax evasion and of handing out favours to a company donating money to his re-election campaign.
Opposition politicians have demanded Dehaene address parliament on the allegations.

One foreign exchange trader said, "I expect we will see some discreet central bank action (to support the franc). I don't expect this to develop into a full-blown crisis. But it will take a statement from Mr Dehaene to get this out of the way."
